title: Introduce blob import path and deterministic manifest compactifier for stable changelogs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a new model intake route that accepts artifact URIs (S3/GCS/HTTP) with provenance verification and a deterministic manifest compactifier that produces stable fingerprints for changelog/delta generation. Improves onboarding reliability and reduces noise in changelogs by emitting checksum-driven diffs.
commits: a1f4d2e: feat(registry): add blob-intake controller and validation hooks
b3c7f91: feat(registry/compact): deterministic manifest serializer and stable-key ordering
c8d9a6b: feat(cli): onboard from-blob subcommand + sample manifest template

description:
Context: We frequently onboard models produced by external tooling where the bundle (weights + tokenizer + metadata) is published to object stores. The current intake path requires manual download and upload; changelog automation picks up non-functional metadata ordering differences which creates noisy release notes. Motivation: Provide a first-class 'blob import' intake path that preserves provenance, verifies checksums, and produces a canonical compact manifest so that changelogs are deterministic and deltas are minimal. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) a blob-intake controller (registry/ingest/blob_intake.py) that accepts an artifact URI, validates signatures/checksums, extracts and normalizes metadata, and emits a provenance ledger entry; and 2) a deterministic manifest compactifier (registry/compact/manifest_compactifier.py) that canonicalizes entries, sorts by stable keys, strips ephemeral probe fields, and computes a manifest fingerprint (sha256) used by changelog/delta generation.

Design notes: The compactifier uses a stable key ordering derived from (artifact_type, name, model_version, architecture, quantization) and falls back to lexicographic sorting for nested maps. Metadata normalization rules are recorded in registry/ingest/validators.py — we normalize datetime formats to RFC3339, canonicalize license fields to SPDX identifiers, and strip transient probe tags unless explicitly marked keep_in_manifest. The blob-intake path supports object store URIs (s3://, gs://) and HTTPS (with optional signed URL). On ingest we compute per-file checksums and a bundle-level manifest checksum; artifacts are not duplicated in storage if the checksum exists (content-addressable behavior). A provenance ledger entry records source_uri, resolved_checksums, importer, import_time, and optional signer_info.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing /onboard endpoints still work. The new onboard-from-blob CLI is optional and introduced under cli/onboard_from_blob.py. To enable the blob intake in existing private deployments, a feature flag registry.blob_intake.enabled was added and defaulted to false; fleet deploys will flip this flag after rollout. A DB migration (migrations/2026_02_add_blob_intake.sql) adds a provenance table. We included a migration utility scripts/migrations/backfill_provenance.py to backfill using recent intake logs (not included in this PR; separate ENG ticket).

Testing: Unit tests added (tests/test_compactifier.py) check deterministic output for a variety of input shapes, including reordering and probe-field noise. Integration tests with an S3 mock (tests/integration/test_blob_ingest_s3mock.py and ci/workflows/registry-e2e.yml) cover end-to-end ingest, dedup, and manifest fingerprint stability across two ingestion runs of the same bundle. CI job uses scripts/s3mock-setup.sh to spin up localstack/s3mock. Performance quick-checks (registry/metrics/manifest_metrics.py) were added to ensure compactifier runtime is O(n log n) with acceptable constants on sample manifests.

Checklist:
- [x] Blob-intake controller with basic validation and checksum verification
- [x] Deterministic manifest compactifier + serializer
- [x] CLI: onboard-from-blob for manual testing
- [x] Unit + integration tests and CI job
- [x] DB migration and feature flag guarded rollout
- [ ] Optional: backfill utility in a follow-up (ENG-5010)

Files changed (high-level): Added new ingestion and compact modules, CLI helper, docs for blob intake and changelog behavior, expanded CI to run S3 mock e2e, added DB migration. See changed_files for a short list. Notable implementation details are commented in registry/compact/serializer.py where we document the canonicalization rules and the manifest fingerprint computation.

Review summary and rationale for squash merge: This PR includes several small commits (implementation + tests + docs). Guarded by a feature flag, and the DB migration is backward-compatible. We prefer squash to keep main history compact while retaining the commit message summary in release notes.

Rollout and observability: Default rollout is feature-flagged, we will enable in staging for one week, monitor manifest_metrics.manifest_compact_time_ms and registry.provenance.ingest_failures. Alert thresholds: >5% ingest failure rate in 24h or median compact_time > 1s for manifests < 1k entries. If observed, roll back feature flag and open ENG-4921 for follow-up.
review_comments: Ethan Brooks (2026-02-13): Nice separation between intake and compactifier. Two asks: (1) can we make the RFC3339 normalization configurable? Some legacy metadata uses custom timezone strings; (2) ensure the compactifier preserves 'display_name' fields even if they are not stable keys. -- requested changes

Maya Patel (2026-02-14): Reply: made timezone normalizer pluggable via registry.config.metadata.normalizers and updated serializer to keep display_name if keep_in_manifest=true. Added unit tests to cover both cases.

Carlos Ruiz (2026-02-17): Minor: in blob_intake.py please return 409 for duplicate checksum instead of 200 to make dedup semantics explicit. -- requested change
Maya Patel (2026-02-17): Reply: updated blob_intake to return 409 for dedup and added docs section 'Dedup semantics' in docs/onboarding/blob-intake.md. CI green after change.
